title: Marion County has weekend of arts and crafts
author: Laura Fowler Paulus
description: Marion County hosted two successful large arts and crafts fairs this past weekend. The fairs, Hillsboro's Arts and Crafts Fair and Marion's Art in the Park, happen annually on the third weekend in…
content:
Tabor College student Hannah Thurston performs for the crowd at the Hillsboro Arts & Crafts Fair on Saturday. Various students performed throughout the day with many singing songs from Tabor's upcoming musical Guys and Dolls -photo by Karrie Rathbone HHS Wrestling returned to the fair with their famous Indian Tacos. They had not served the popular food since 2019. The booth was just one of many food booths run by local organizations. There were plenty of options for everyone—photo by Karrie Rathbone.For more photos of the Hillsboro Arts & Crafts Fair, visit https://rathboneimages.pixieset.com/artsandcraftsfair/. HHS students Addison Jost and Quinlyn Funk worked a shift emptying garbage cans. It takes many volunteers from all over the community to pull off a successful fai—photo by Karrie Rathbone. Hillsboro Police Chief Jessey Hiebert and Officer Duane McCarty pose for a quick photo while keeping order at the fair. People of all ages flooded downtown Hillsboro on Saturday to enjoy food and shopping—photo by Karrie Rathbone. David Loewen, Joanne Loewen and Tena Loewen ready for the crowd at Saturday's fair. They had a steady stream of customers looking for a refreshing treat in the heat. Rodney Bates, of Strong City, played some music and sang for the crowd on Saturday at Marion's Art in the Park. Marion had 150 vendor booths at their annual Art in the Park. The event is on the third Saturday and Sunday every September.
Marion County hosted two successful large arts and crafts fairs this past weekend. The fairs, Hillsboro's Arts and Crafts Fair and Marion's Art in the Park, happen annually on the third weekend in September. Hillsboro's fair is on Saturday while Art in the Park is on Saturday and Sunday.
Hillsboro's Arts and Crafts Fair
Since its creation in 1970, The Hillsboro Arts & Crafts Fair has been rated among the top 100 arts and crafts shows in the country according to Sunshine Artist magazine.
This year was the fair's 55th anniversary so even more effort was put into it.
'I think every year the board does an amazing job at getting the word out, but being an anniversary this year it was wonderful seeing everyone give a little more. One of our board members, Amanda Jaworsky, did an amazing job of handling many of the artistic aspects of the fair. She printed commemorative t-shirts for our board members and made 55th-anniversary water bottle stickers that were available for free at the information booth. Baker Brothers Printing came up with a modern new design for our logo and supplied us with a new window graphic for our office space, new highway billboard signage and printed the food and information flyers. Our Hillsboro Public Library started a children's crafting time this year, and I hope to see that grow and continue in the following years. Holli Carter did a great job with social media and other advertising for this year's 55th event. And Caitlyn Hall, our board president, had an amazing interview with KAKE news,' said Director Jill Bailey.
There were 226 vendors this year with a total of 341 booth spaces.
'That doesn't include the 24 local food vendors we had. We also had many shoppers stop at the information booth inquiring about being a vendor next year. So it's great to see so much interest and watch our numbers increase,' said Bailey.
While it is difficult to know exactly how many attended the fair, the Hillsboro Police Department (HPD) reported that there were more vendors this year and the number of shoppers attending the event appeared to be higher than last year. The shopping rush took place between the hours of 9 a.m. and 1 p.m.
Bailey credits the successful fair to the many people who helped including HPD, Ben Steketee, Emergency Management Director Marcy Hostetler, Chris Glanzer, the City of Hillsboro, the Hillsboro Chamber of Commerce, The Arts & Crafts Fair Board, and more.
'The fair went spectacularly! I know if it wasn't for the hard work and dedication of past directors it would not have run as smoothly. I am so grateful to have had a wonderful starting point with tried and true procedures in place, as well as a supportive community who wasn't afraid to jump in and help,' said Bailey. 'There is so much that goes into coordinating the event, not just for myself and of the community, but also for the vendors themselves. It's wonderful seeing everyone come together! The fair is a perfect mix of mayhem and order, and if all goes well, they both cancel each other out in the end.'
Bailey is already thinking about next year's fair.
'There are some things I would personally love to see happen for next year such as a virtual application, expanded children's area and more extensive mapping, but sometimes it can take more than a few years to see things come into fruition,' said Bailey. 'The highlights of feedback we received from volunteers, the public and craft vendors had to do with parking options, help with loading and unloading of vendor's craft items, scooter and wheelchair availability, providing a detailed map of all of the craft vendors, food truck options and last but not least we had many requests for a beer garden.'
Bailey welcomes feedback about the event including any ideas or changes people want to see. She also welcomes hearing from anyone who would like to help in the future. Her email is director@hillsboroartsandcraftsfair.org.
Marion's Art in the Park
Judy Christensen served as the Chairman of Art in the Park when it started 46 years ago.
'She started it all those years ago. Then almost 10 years after Hillsboro started their Arts & Crafts Fair, she got Hillsboro and Marion to do them on the same day. It was hard to convince everyone at first and many said it would never work,' said current Art in the Park Chairman Margo Yates.
Christensen knew it would work because she had been an exhibitor in Arkansas where they had more than one fair at a time.
'It's a huge show. And every little town around joined in so you could go to five little towns. I saw how good that worked for them so I came back to get Marion and Hillsboro going the same day. I guaranteed everyone that people will hit both shows since they were just 10 miles apart,' said Christensen. 'They now understand. People make the drive further since they have two places to go. It's been good for everybody. It hasn't taken anything away from either one of them.'
Christensen still enjoys helping out with the event.
'I'm now 83, and here I still am,' said Christensen. Judy Christensen and Margo Yates. Christensen served as Marion's Art in the Park Chairman since it started. She served in the role for over forty years and has been on the committee for 46 years.Yates took over as Chairman four years ago.
Yates has served as chairman since Christensen stepped down four years ago. That is when they added Sunday to the event making it a two-day fair.
'I started years ago as the assistant and they moved me up. We went for it and added Sunday. You never know until you try something,' said Yates.
Yates said that having two days has been successful.
'Vendors like it. I went to the ministers first and made sure nobody would be upset. I told one minister who was worried that people wouldn't come to church to tell them to come to the park after church and get lunch and shop. So it worked well,' said Yates. 'Last year, I talked to all the vendors on Sunday and everybody was happy. One vendor had a sale for $1,000 last year on Sunday. So it seems to be growing and doing okay.'
The event had 150 vendors this year.
'I recruit every year and try to get a good variety of different things and make it fun,' said Yates.
'She's so good with all her experience and skills,' said Christensen. 'She knows customer service is important. It makes a big difference. And she has such a good attitude.'
'Well, you can't do it without all this help. And some of the volunteers have helped for decades. It takes a lot of people to pull this off,' said Yates. 'And the FFA students stay down here at night so we have security Friday and Saturday nights. With the weather Friday night, they were making sure everybody's stuff was okay.'
Yates appreciated the nice weather on Saturday which allowed for a large crowd at the event. The crowd was smaller due to the weather on Sunday, but many vendors still did well.
'The crowd's been picking up these last few years. You just never know what's gonna happen with numbers,' said Yates. 'Our numbers are up, and it's been a good, big year.'

title: Lifelong Bluebird settles into new role
author: Laura Fowler Paulus
description: Jody Schmidt has been a Bluebird for much of her life. The new principal at Goessel Elementary School grew up in the USD 411 Goessel School District and graduated from Goessel High School. She also…
content:
Jayce, Javin, Jody, Craig, Jayley and Jerah Schmidt. Jody is the new principal at Goessel Elementary School.
Jody Schmidt has been a Bluebird for much of her life. The new principal at Goessel Elementary School grew up in the USD 411 Goessel School District and graduated from Goessel High School. She also spent the last 23 years teaching at Goessel Elementary School before becoming the principal there this fall.
'Shortly after the birth of our first child, my husband and I decided to move home to Goessel as we wanted our children to experience the opportunities a small school has to offer. Goessel schools provide students with a well-rounded education while offering students many opportunities to be involved. The wonderful students, outstanding families, exceptional staff and supportive community is amazing,' said Schmidt.
After graduating from Goessel High School. Schmidt attended Tabor College where she earned her Elementary Education and Special Education degrees. She then earned a Masters of Science in Educational Administration from Emporia State University.
Schmidt began her career in education as an employee of the Harvey County Special Education Cooperative.
'My teaching assignment was at Halstead Middle School as one of the 4th through 8th grade special education teachers in the building,' said Schmidt.
After three years at Halstead Middle School, she began working for the Marion County Special Education Cooperative teaching special education at Goessel Elementary and did that for the next 23 years before moving to the role of principal.
Schmidt thoroughly enjoyed her time as a special education teacher and wasn't looking to leave the role.
'I enjoyed facilitating student growth and the positive relationships I built with students, parents and staff. I am passionate about advocating for students and their families to ensure the best education for all. However, when the elementary principalship opened up, I realized this opportunity would allow me to positively impact a greater number of students and families, support the outstanding staff and give back to a community that has given so much to me,' said Schmidt.
The position became open when Superintendent Mark Crawford shifted to only doing the superintendent role.
'I was the elementary principal and superintendent for three years at Goessel. I am now a half-time superintendent. Our BOE wanted this to be a cost-neutral initiative. My salary was cut by more than 50% to provide a fair principal wage for Mrs. Schmidt. Our district-level work force is very bare bones, even compared to other 1A districts. This empowers us to have a healthy number of teachers and staff dedicated to the classroom,' said Crawford.
Even with all of her experience in education, Schmidt has found there is a lot to learn in her new position.
'As a veteran special education teacher, I was quite comfortable and knowledgeable in my role and responsibilities. As a first-year administrator, it's like being a first-year teacher all over again,' said Schmidt. 'However I have thoroughly enjoyed the new learning and have worked hard to positively impact those around me. I am blessed to work with amazing people here at Goessel. I am particularly thankful for the support I've received from my fellow Goessel administrators, the Goessel Elementary staff, the office team and the USD 411 Board of Education.'
She has been surprised at the sheer number of decisions there are to make in a typical school day as principal but she enjoys the job.
'As principal, I enjoy building relationships with students, helping students succeed, celebrating success and promoting a positive school culture. I also enjoy supporting and positively impacting staff members. Working with parents and community members is also extremely rewarding,' said Schmidt.
'Mrs. Jody Schmidt is an instructional leader. Her many years as a teacher providing specialized instruction gives her a unique skill set as a new building leader. She understands the science of reading and what high-quality pedagogy looks like in all subjects. The most powerful, yet simple leadership trait she has earned is the trust of her teachers. She is a great listener and she knows what the staff and students need,' said Crawford.
Schmidt has several goals for the year.
'This school year I want to continue the tradition of excellence at Goessel Elementary. I plan to work to ensure students excel academically and socially. It is important that each student and staff member feel valued and supported in our school community. I also plan to continue to develop my leadership skills and engage in new learning as we are all lifelong learners,' said Schmidt.
Schmidt has been happily married for 26 years to her husband Craig. They have four children Jayce, Javin, Jayley and Jerah and a daughter-in-law named Danielle.
'We are both Goessel grads and attended Goessel Schools from Kindergarten through 12th grade. Together we have four children. Three of our four children are Goessel grads and our youngest is currently attending Goessel High School,' said Schmidt.
When not at school, Schmidt enjoys spending time with her family.
'Supporting my children as they participate in school activities has been a hobby over the years. I also enjoy reading and baking,' said Schmidt.

title: Be aware: scams are on the rise
author: Hillsboro Free Press
description: The City of Hillsboro recently sent out a warning to let people know they need to be aware of scams. 'We've had people get text messages regarding taking a survey for the city. They are taking…
content:
The City of Hillsboro recently sent out a warning to let people know they need to be aware of scams.
'We've had people get text messages regarding taking a survey for the city. They are taking advantage of our lead and copper survey that we've sent out to try and get residents to click on fraudulent links,' said Hillsboro City Administrator Matt Stiles.
In addition to texts, the scammers have been using emails and phone calls.
'We regularly have people contacted to pay utility bills over the phone, which is something we never do. Those calls typically target our senior citizens but sometimes others. There is so much increased activity happening right now it's a little overwhelming,' said Stiles. 'The city has taken a lot of proactive steps to prevent those types of things, but at the end of the day, people are human and people looking to take advantage can be persuasive.'
Marion Police Chief Zach Hudlin said that last week they had a resident tell them she received a call saying there was a tax warrant she needed to pay or the police would be there to arrest her.
'Thankfully she knew it was a scam and did not give them any information,' said Hudlin.
Hudlin said he received a text last week saying he had an overdue toll from the turnpike that was a scam.
The scammers aren't just attacking individuals. Stiles said there have also been attempts to spoof city staff emails internally, but those haven't affected the public.
He also said the CISA (Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency) sent out a warning last week to public utilities about increased attacks on public infrastructure.
'Those attempts are mostly targeting control devices in systems, like valves or transformers, not customers. We don't have a lot of capabilities to remotely screw up operations and what we do have is secured and has alarms to notify us about changes. Still, you have to treat those threats as real and take steps to keep the bad guys out,' said Stiles.
The FBI has also warned against a jump in fraudulent online activity driven by the upcoming election and conflicts around the world.
'Do not click on suspicious links or provide any personal information. When in doubt, give us a call at City Hall at 620-947-3162,' said Stiles.
'If someone suspects that a call/text/email is a scam, they should call dispatch to report it to the police department,' said Hudlin.

title: Area Sports Roundup 10.02.24
author: Hillsboro Free Press
description: Goessel Volleyball – The Bluebirds went 2-0 on Tuesday, Sept. 24 in league action at home. Scores were as follows: Goessel defeated Wakefield 25-6, 25-8; Goessel defeated Rural Vista 25-5, 25-8. The…
content:
Owen Dalke scores on a pick 6 to bring the final score in the Hillsboro/Halstead game to 27-0 at Friday night's Homecoming game.
Goessel
Volleyball – The Bluebirds went 2-0 on Tuesday, Sept. 24 in league action at home. Scores were as follows: Goessel defeated Wakefield 25-6, 25-8; Goessel defeated Rural Vista 25-5, 25-8.
The Goessel volleyball team went 5-0 on Saturday, Sept. 28 at the Olpe Round Robin Tournament. Scores were as follows: Goessel defeated Madison 25-9, 25-10; Goessel defeated Wabaunsee 25-19, 25-20; Goessel defeated Northern Heights 25-8, 25-8; Goessel defeated Olpe 25-9, 25-16;
Goessel defeated Bishop Seabury 25-5, 25-13.
'This is the 2nd year in a row Goessel has won the Olpe Tournament. The Goessel JV tournament also went 4-0 today to take the Olpe JV division championship,' said Coach Crystal Guhr.
Goessel Varsity's overall record moves to 19-2 on the season.
Coming—The Bluebirds will compete at St. Xavier on Monday, Oct. 7.
Hillsboro
Cross-country – The Trojans competed at the Marion meet on Thursday, Sept. 26.
'We had some great runs today at Marion,' said Coach Brielle Loewen.
For the Trojan girls, Quinlyn Funk took first place with a time of 20:47, Riley Richert placed 3rd at 20:52, Jaidyn Frantz was 10th at 23:46, Nora Hein came in at 28:55 and Gabi Sibayan finished in a time of 39:22.
Wyatt Dies had a great PR at 21:32 coming in first for the boys, then Ben Werner with a PR of 23:09 and Elijah Holmes in 28:45.
Coming—The team will compete on Thursday, Oct. 3 at Winfield.
Football – The Trojans had their homecoming game against Halstead on Friday, Sept. 27. Hillsboro won with a final score of 27-0.
After a 0-0 half, Hillsboro came out swinging in the second half with 14 points in the third quarter. The scoring got started with a Zayne Haslett 5-yard run to go up 7-0. Haslett got back in the endzone just a few minutes later with an 11-yard run to put Hillsboro up 14-0.
In the fourth, Jesiah Gooch punched a score in from 10 yards out with 5:50 left in the fourth quarter, and with just one minute left in the game Owen Dalke put Hillsboro up 27-0 with a pick-six interception.
Coming—The Trojans next play on Friday, Oct. 4 at Ellsworth.
Tennis – The Trojan girls played Lyons last week in a double dual on Monday, Sept. 23.
Cassidy Bernhardt played the #1 singles. She lost to Kendal Webb(Lyons) 4-6 and defeated Mylee Smith (Nickerson) 6-1.
'After a tough first-round loss, Cassidy bounced back and won her second singles match. She took control of the match early and never looked back. She played consistent and solid in that match,' said Coach David Ediger.
For #1 doubles, Claire Morey and Maylee Hardey took 1st place. They defeated Nevaeh Becker and Isabel Gonzalez (Lyons) 7-6 (2). They also defeated Kyleigh Hathaway and Amelia Kinast (Nickerson) 6-1.
'Claire and Maylee showed a lot of grit in their first match, winning in a tie-breaker and they dominated their second match of the day for the 1st place finish,' said Ediger.
For #2 singles, Claire Morey lost to Nevaeh Becker (Lyons) 7-6 (4) and defeated Brecken Kelmun (Nickerson) 6-1.
'Claire played really well in singles. She was down 2-5 in her first match, battled back to take a 6-5 lead, then couldn't quite hold on in the tie-breaker. In her second match, she got ahead early and finished strong. She was very consistent in her singles play,' said Ediger.
Maylee Harder played the #3 singles. She lost to Karson Peter (Lyons) 4-6 and defeated Kyleigh Hathaway (Nickerson) 6-2.
'Maylee did a really good job during her singles play. She could have easily won her first match as she was in every game. She did an outstanding job in her second singles match, earning the win,' said Ediger.
The Trojan girls next hosted an invitational at home on Thursday, Sept. 26. They finished in 7th place out of 8 teams. Classical of Wichita took 1st place in the tournament.
'Overall it was a very tough meet with several good players and teams. I was proud of our girls and the effort they all gave,' said Ediger.
Hardey and Morey had chances in their second doubles match. Tied at 6-6, they took a 30-love lead in a critical game but couldn't quite put the game away and ended up falling 8-6.
'If they would have gone ahead 7-6, I think they could have won the match. They did respond well in the final match of the day for an 8-0 victory,' said Ediger.
Bernhardt had a back-and-forth match in her second match of the day. She played well but came up just short, dropping that one 8-6.
'Cassidy played well all day long making a few adjustments during the tournament. She finished off the day with an 8-2 victory,' said Ediger.
Coming—The team will close out the regular season with the league meet in Hillsboro on Saturday, Oct. 5.
Volleyball – It was a busy week for the Hillsboro High School volleyball team as they competed in their second league night at Halstead on Tuesday, Sept. 24 and then traveled to Douglass for a tournament on Saturday, Sept. 28.
The Trojans came home Tuesday night with a win and loss, beating Nickerson but losing to host team Halstead. The week ended on a high note as the Trojans went 5-0 on Saturday to win the Douglas Invitational Tournament.
In the first contest of the evening on Tuesday, the Trojans faced the Nickerson Panthers. It was the first meeting for the two teams this season. Hillsboro rolled to a 25-12 first-game win but found themselves in a battle in the second game. Coming from behind Hillsboro clawed their way back in behind the serving of sophomore Daisy Klein to tie the game at 22. The score then see-sawed back and forth the rest of the game. Tied at 24, Hillsboro called a timeout. Nickerson then missed the next serve to give the Trojans a one-point advantage. Hillsboro sealed the game with a kill on the next play. Juniors Kingzley Ratzlaff, Lauryn Vogt and Talia Jost led the way with 13,10 and 6 kills respectively.
In the late game, Hillsboro took on the host Halstead Dragons. Halstead used an array of attackers and tough serving to beat the Trojans in the first set 25-15. The second set started differently and Hillsboro also used constant attacking and tough serving to build an early lead. The Dragons would not go away, pushed their way back into the lead and never let it go. It was the first league loss of the season for the Trojans.
The final scores were: Hillsboro defeated Nickerson 25-12, 26-24; Halstead defeated Hillsboro 25-15, 25-22.
'The girls did some good things against Nickerson. I was happy the way they came back from a deficit in the second game to win it. Of course, we are disappointed in the Halstead loss, but they are a good team and we learned a lot about ourselves and more areas that we need to improve. We will use this to drive us to improve as we continue our season,' said Coach Sandy Arnold.
On Saturday, Sept. 28, Hillsboro traveled to Douglass for their third tournament of the season. In pool play, Hillsboro faced Eldorado, Douglass and Leon-Bluestem. The Trojans played consistent volleyball with some sound passing, constant attacking and tough serving to win each match in two sets. Vogt had five aces in the Douglass contest and Ella Potucek handed out 17 assists. The Trojans continued to use tough serving to keep Douglass out of system. This time it was Amyah Werth who dropped in six aces.
In the semi-finals, Hillsboro was matched up against Augusta. Several Trojans went on serving streaks in the match to limit Augusta's offense. Vogt, Potucek, Skylar Voran, Ratzlaff and Werth all went on 4-8 point runs for Hillsboro at different points in the match.
In the finals, the Trojans met their toughest opponent of the day in the Garden Plain Owls. Garden Plain has a strong volleyball tradition and program. In the first set it was again Hillsboro's serving and constant attack that proved the difference for the Trojans as they did not let the Owls get much set up in the game. Garden Plain, however, made some adjustments before game two and built an early lead at 10-4. It was Hillsboro who then had to make adjustments and they fought their way back into the game—only to see the Owls make another run and go up 24-19. The Trojans never quit and served their way back to 23-24 before Garden Plain sealed the win with a kill and forced a third and deciding set.
In the final set, Hillsboro worked their way to a small two-point lead and then extended that lead to five behind the serving of Ratzlaff. Hillsboro maintained that lead to the 21-16 point when Ratzlaff returned to the service line and helped the Trojans increase the lead to eight—the point difference at the end of the final set.
The final scores were: Hillsboro defeated Eldorado 25-14, 25-11; Hillsboro defeated Douglass 25-7, 25-6; Hillsboro defeated Leon-Bluestem 25-9, 25-13; Hillsboro defeated Augusta 25-5, 25-9; Hillsboro defeated Garden Plain 25-14, 23-25, 25-17.
Hillsboro's Lauryn Vogt, Kingsley Ratzlaff and Amyah Werth were all named to the Douglass All-Tournament team.
'I was very proud of the girls for the way they played throughout the day. First, it was the day after Homecoming, and second, we were late to the tournament due to an unforeseen detour and a train delay. I thought the girls played each match at their level and that was important going into the finals because we knew Garden Plain was going to be a tough opponent. They have good athletes and they are very well-coached. The girls made good adjustments throughout the match—particularly the last two sets—to find new ways to score and they also did some great things defensively that we haven't done as much of up to this point. It was a good way to end the week,' said Arnold.
Coming—The Trojans will compete on Thursday, Oct. 8 at Smoky Valley.
Marion
Cross-country – The team competed in their home meet on Thursday, Sept. 26.
'What a day for our Wildcat and Warrior runners. It was a great showing at our home meet,' said Coach Jason Hett.
For the varsity girls, Izy Branson had a great race with a PR time on the season.
'She medaled in 12th place, and she is learning the 5K race,' said Hett.
Brooklyn Beery attacked the day and finished in 5th place with a great time.
'She is getting stronger from two to three miles and it showed today,' said Hett.
For the varsity boys, the team was led by Luke Wessel who took home gold.
'He set the pace for the whole race and never looked back,' said Hett.
Eli Klenda placed 6th with a season-best time.
Harrison Beery medaled in 15th, Zayden Janzen medaled in 18th and Owen White in 19th.
Keenan Lange ran a season-best time and competed well placing 30.
'Josh Smith rounded us out today and will look to continue to push for spot seven,' said Hett. 'The boys captured the team title today for the 4th year in a row. Hard work pays off! We had a great week of practice and challenged them this week and it showed up today in how they ran! Proud of this group. They know the work is not done yet.'
Coming—The team will compete on Thursday, Oct. 3 at Halstead.

title: Deadline extended for summer EBT benefit
author: Jessie Wagoner
description: By Jessie Wagoner Families needing food assistance have additional time to apply for the Summer EBT program through Kansas Department of Children and Families (DCF). The program provides $120 per…
content:
By Jessie Wagoner
Families needing food assistance have additional time to apply for the Summer EBT program through Kansas Department of Children and Families (DCF). The program provides $120 per eligible child in food assistance to assist families.
Summer EBT is a partnership between DCF, the U.S. Dept. of Agriculture, Food and Nutrition Services and the Kansas Department of Education. It launched in July of 2024 to provide families with a one-time benefit to buy groceries over the summer when food insecurity increases among school-aged children.
DCF said since July 2024, approximately 117,200 school-aged children have received the $120 Summer EBT benefit. Most of those received it through an auto-issuance program for families already receiving EBT benefits. DCF reports they have received 2,000 additional applications, but they expect many more children to qualify for the benefit.
' We estimate there could be more than 100,000 children who did not automatically receive the benefit but may be eligible,' DCF stated in a news release.
Dale Armstrong of Sedgwick said the program was a 'life-saver' for his family of six over the summer. He used the funds to purchase non-perishable and frozen foods his children could eat throughout the summer.
' I stocked up on ground beef, chicken, canned fruit and veggies,' Armstrong said. 'With four kids, they go through a lot of food, and it was a relief to be able to have some frozen items to carry us through.'
Children may be eligible for the program if they attended a Kansas school offering the National School Lunch or School Breakfast Program and the household income met the requirements for free or reduced-price school meals at any point during the 2023-2024 school year.
' I thought the program was only for people who were already receiving EBT,' Megan Colby of rural Harvey County said. 'Now that I know, I'll be applying for my three kids. $360 would be really helpful for groceries.'
Families with children who did not receive the Summer EBT benefit by the end of July 2024 should apply through the online self-service portal, dcfapp.kees.ks.gov. The application deadline is 5 p.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 15.
' While Summer EBT is intended to help offset the cost of food during summer break when kids don't have access to the free or reduced-price meals they get at school, even with children already back in class, the program can still provide families with a little extra help in putting food on their tables,' DCF Secretary Laura Howard said. 'We hope that by extending the application deadline, more families with eligible children will have the opportunity to apply for this year's Summer EBT benefit.'

title: County rejects 30x30 resolution
author: Laura Fowler Paulus
description: The Marion County Board of Commissioners met on Monday, Oct. 7 where they discussed the resolution opposing the federal government's 30x30 land preservation goal which seeks to preserve 30% of the…
content:
The Marion County Board of Commissioners met on Monday, Oct. 7 where they discussed the resolution opposing the federal government's 30×30 land preservation goal which seeks to preserve 30% of the nation's land and water by 2030.
The board, Planning and Zoning Director Sharon Omstead and County Counselor Brad Jantz have been working on the resolution since April after it was brought to the board by Commissioner Kent Becker. Becker, who refers to the 30×30 land preservation goal as a 'land grab', has been pushing the resolution since hearing about it from a speaker at a Patriots for Liberty of Marion County, KS meeting.
The board held a public meeting on Monday, Sept. 30 to hear from the public about the resolution. 23 people attended the meeting. Only five spoke at the meeting and all expressed support for the resolution.
The resolution stated the board supports the continued private and exclusive ownership of land in the county and recognizes and supports the State of Kansas's laws governing water rights and water use. It also stated that any land acquired under the 30×30 program should be acquired from willing landowners and compensation should equal the fair market value of all rights and interests acquired.
The resolution also stated that the board opposes the designation of Marion County land as part of the 30×30 program and reserves the right to analyze and consider the impact of each permanent easement executed in Marion County.
After a brief discussion on Monday, Oct. 7, the board rejected the resolution (3-2) with Commissioners Dave Crofoot, Dave Mueller and Randy Dallke voting against it and Becker and Commissioner Jonah Gehring voting for it.
County Clerk Ashley Herpich reminded the board that Tuesday, Oct. 15 is the last day to register to vote.
The board will next meet on Tuesday, Oct. 15.

title: Area Sports Roundup 10.16.24
author: Hillsboro Free Press
description: Goessel Volleyball – The Bluebirds defeated Centre in the final league match of the season on Tuesday, Oct. 8. Scores were as follows 25-12, 25-14, 25-9. Goessel resumed play on Saturday, Oct. 12 in…
content:
Hillsboro's Lauryn Vogt hits the ball against Haven on Saturday, Oct. 12 in the home invitational.
Goessel
Volleyball – The Bluebirds defeated Centre in the final league match of the season on Tuesday, Oct. 8. Scores were as follows 25-12, 25-14, 25-9.
Goessel resumed play on Saturday, Oct. 12 in the Wheat State League Tournament. They went 3-2 and finished 3rd. Scores were as follows: Goessel defeated Solomon 25-11, 25-9;
Herington defeated Goessel 22-25, 18-25; Goessel defeated Centre 25-10, 25-12; Goessel defeated Elyria 25-8, 25-21; Little River defeated Goessel 25-16, 25-22.
Goessel moves to 27-7 overall.
Coming—The Bluebirds will compete in regional playoffs on Tuesday, Oct. 22.
Hillsboro
Cross-country – The Trojans competed at Sterling on Thursday, Oct. 10.
'We had some great races at the Sterling meet,' said Coach Brielle Loewen.
Leading the Trojan girls was Riley Richert in 2nd place with a great PR of 19:44 which also knocked down the old school record.
Quinlyn Funk came in 5th place in 20:11.9 (PR), Jaidyn Frantz was 13th with a time of 21:24.2 (PR), Anna King 27:57.9 (PR), Nora Hein 28:59.0 and Gabi Sibayan 36:06.4 (PR).
Leading the boys was Wyatt Dies with a PR of 21:01.1, Ben Werner followed with a PR of 23:00.4, Casen Steinert came in at 23:42.7 and Elijah Holmes in 26:35.7.
Coming—The Trojans will next compete at on Thursday, Oct. 17 in Larned.
Volleyball – It was a busy week for the Hillsboro High School Volleyball team. The team played nine matches in five days.
The Trojans started their week on Tuesday, Oct. 8, at Smoky Valley for their last league triangular. Hillsboro defeated Haven in the first match of the evening but it wasn't without a fight by the Wildcats. Haven held the lead a couple of times before Hillsboro could make a comeback and seal the victory with a 25-23 win in the final game.
In the final contest of the evening the Trojans took on the host team, the Smoky Valley Vikings. The first meeting between the two teams was a battle to the finish and this one turned out to be the same. With each team winning close games, it came down to the final set. It was back and forth the entire game as the lead switched hands many times. In the end, Smoky Valley was able to put down the final point to win the game and match 28-26. Lauryn Vogt and Kingzley Ratzlaff both recorded 15 kills, while Ella Potucek assisted in 32 kills and Amyah Werth dug up 29 balls. The Trojans ended up in 4th place in the CKL.
The final scores were as follows: Hillsboro defeated Haven 25-17, 25-23; Smoky Valley defeated Hillsboro 25-22, 20-25, 26-28.
'Once again our league was incredibly tough this season. There were different upsets throughout the league allowing for no undefeated teams. Many of the teams have a great shot at going a long way in the post-season. It is our hope that the strength of our league will only make us stronger as we head into post-season play,' said Coach Sandy Arnold.
On Thursday, Oct. 10, the Trojans traveled to play in a competitive non-league triangular in Great Bend. There they would face the hometown Panthers as well as the Emporia Spartans. Hillsboro found themselves in another battle that went down to the wire in their first contest with Emporia. Hillsboro won the first game, but the Spartans battled back to take game two. Despite holding a 5-point advantage for most of the third set, Hillsboro could not hold off an Emporia comeback to even out the score. From that point on the game went back and forth until the Trojans were able to finalize the win at 25-23. Vogt led the Trojans with 21 kills. Potucek added 36 assists and Werth picked up 22 hits.
In the late match of the evening, Hillsboro faced state-ranked Great Bend. It was a tough matchup for the young Trojans. The Panthers jumped out with an early lead but the Trojans fought their way back to within one at 17-18 before Great Bend shut the door and won 18-25. The Panthers took care of business in the second game with a solid 25-13 win over the Trojans.
The scores were as follows: Hillsboro defeated Emporia 25-18, 18-25, 25-23; Great Bend defeated Hillsboro 25-18, 25-13.
'This triangular always proves to be very competitive for us. We feel it is a great way to make us better in the long run. I am proud of the girls for the way they hung on in the match against Emporia when they made their run on us. We need these matches to test our mental and emotional abilities as well as our skills,' said Arnold.
The Trojans hosted their Hillsboro Invitational on Saturday, Oct. 12—a week earlier this season due to a change in the post-season format. As a result, the format for the tournament was also different. Since two teams could not come because of the change in the date, the tournament consisted of only six teams instead of eight. Instead of pool and bracket play then, a round robin format was used.
Hillsboro began their day facing the Haven Wildcats for the third time this season. Despite finding themselves facing an eight-point deficit early in game one, the Trojans continued to claw their way out of the hole and ended up taking the first game 25-21. Hillsboro controlled the second game from the beginning and never let up, winning 25-6.
In their second contest of the day, Hillsboro took on the CKL league champs and state-ranked Halstead Dragons. Hillsboro battled hard in the first game but could not get enough shots to fall on the scrappy Dragons. Halstead took the first game 25-22. Unfortunately, the Trojans could not get things rolling in the second game and Halstead went on to a relatively easy win, 25-13.
The third opponent on the day was the Irish from Chapman. Hillsboro used strong serving runs from Vogt, Daisy Klein and Skylar Voran, who had three aces in a row. The Trojans took the match 25-15, 25-9.
Minneapolis was the next opponent for the Trojans. Hillsboro held off the Lions in the first game with more tough serving. Potucek and Voran both went on runs to take the Lions out of their game. The final score of set one was 25-14. Minneapolis did not back down, however, and challenged the Trojans—even taking a 16-13 lead. Down 19-21, Vogt took over at the serving line and finished the game for Hillsboro with six straight serves to win it 25-21.
In the final match of the tournament, Hillsboro faced the only undefeated team of the day in Rock Creek. A 4A powerhouse, Rock Creek jumped out to an early 12-6 lead in the first set. The Trojans showed a lot of grit, slowly working their way back into the game. With the score at 12-19, Klein took over at the service line and scored five straight points to pull the team within two. The Trojans cut the lead to one but could not add the finishing touches and Rock Creek took the first game 25-23. The second game started similarly to the first as the Mustangs took an early 8-0 lead. Hillsboro did not give up and slowly battled their way back. Behind 6-12, Werth led the charge from the serving line scoring seven points before Rock Creek could sideout. The momentum swung back and forth the rest of the game before Rock Creek sealed another 23-25 win.
Hillsboro ended the day with a 3-2 record and a third-place finish at the invitational. Their overall record stands at 22-11.
'It was a full day of volleyball for our girls after a busy week of volleyball. I am proud of the girls for the determination they showed throughout the day. There were many times we were in really big holes, but they never gave up and either came back and won or came back to challenge talented and athletic teams to the very end. The girls did a lot of things well today. They followed the game plan, listened to their coaches and teammates to find ways to score and, most importantly, never gave up on the game plan or each other. This group has grown tremendously since the beginning of the season. We have grown in our skills as well as our volleyball IQ. Hopefully they have also grown in their confidence in themselves and each other.
Coming—The Trojans have one more night of regular season action on Thursday, Oct. 17 in Marion, where they will face the Warriors as well as the Lebo Wolves. Postseason play starts on Monday, Oct. 21. The new format this year has all teams playing in regionals before heading to sub-state.
Marion
Cross-country – Marion competed at the Goessel Invitational in North Newton on Thursday, Oct. 10.
'This has become one of our favorite meets of the season,' said Coach Jason Hett.
High school varsity girls were led by Brooklyn Beery who medaled in 9th place.
'She was just off her PR, and she will have a big couple of weeks coming,' said Hett.
Izy Branson placed 25th.
'I know she was a bit frustrated with her time, but had a great finish,' said Hett.
Luke Wessel led the varsity boys with a strong race and finish placing 2nd.
'He is looking stronger and is ready to make the final push,' said Hett. 'Eli Klenda ran a strong race coming in 7th. These two continue to lead this group these next few weeks.'
Zayden Janzen placed 21st, just missing a medal, but continues to break his wall and push each week. 'He has really stepped up this season and will need too again to finish the season,' said Hett. 'Harrison Beery placed 25th and we will look to him to shave some time off these next 2 weeks to push this group. Keenan Lange placed 38th and Jaxon Salsbury 39th to solidify their spots these next two weeks.'
Josh Smith rounded out varsity by placing 42nd.
'The boys took home 2nd place as a team today. It was great to see some of our competition today that we will see next week at league and the following at Regionals. We know where we need to be and the next couple of weeks we will continue to work to finish strong and break the wall,' said Hett.
Coming—Marion will next compete on Thursday, Oct. 17 at Harvey County East Lake Park for the HOA League meet.

title: Goessel School Board listens to high school students
author: Cynthia Goerzen
description: The Goessel school board met on Oct. 14 and listened to five high school seniors who came to the board meeting as part of an assignment for a government class. They expressed appreciation for the wide…
content:
The Goessel school board met on Oct. 14 and listened to five high school seniors who came to the board meeting as part of an assignment for a government class. They expressed appreciation for the wide variety of activities offered by the school and noted that nearly every student is involved in something. The students also had suggestions for more opportunities, such as pottery, art clubs, fishing, archery and other outdoor hobbies. They proposed adding baseball as a high school sport, noting that baseball fields are available. The students expressed appreciation for esports, which is a new opportunity this school year. Junior high/high school principal Scott Boden said the high school esports club plays Fortnite and Super Smash Bros. Six students are participating. Students cannot be in both esports and athletic sports because both practice at the same time.
The students asked for a formalized designated parking space for seniors. They would also like more of a distinction between high school and junior high spaces, especially the Nest, which is a room for students who are feeling stressed. High school students would like their own space.
They also said they would like more emphasis on mental health and suggested adding a mental health class. They would like to destigmatize help for mental health.
The students thanked the board for their support. Board members commended the students for their presentation.
Turning their attention to another matter, the board listened to Becky Suderman, coordinator of Marion County Parents As Teachers, which is part of a nationwide PAT program that offers in-home support for young children from birth to age three. Suderman has been with PAT for 17 years.
Suderman said the families get at least one in-home visit a month for at least an hour. Children are screened for hearing, vision, and development. Parents are offered resources for help. Parents are given ideas for things to do with their children and are shown how to make homemade toys.
Suderman said Marion County PAT is for any young child in the boundaries of the county schools. It is a free service. She said Goessel currently has five families involved, with seven children.
PAT offers group connections that include Big Truck Night, also a CPR class and instruction on choking prevention.
In other business, the board:
* introduced new 5th grade teacher Elizabeth Alderfer. She is a Goessel and Bethel College graduate, did her student teaching at Hesston and was a long-term substitute teacher at Goessel last school year.
* voted to hire Kelli Willis as part-time junior high/high school custodian and Krista Graber as junior high Quiz Bowl sponsor.
* heard from Superintendent Mark Crawford about a letter from the Kansas State Department of Education noting the school's recognition in the 2024 Kansans Can Star Program. Goessel received Gold recognition for Graduation, Bronze for Postsecondary Effectiveness and Copper for being Academically Prepared for Postsecondary.
* heard from Boden that 24 juniors and seniors are earning dual high school/college credit in a total of 116 college credit hours. Boden also mentioned Oct. 30 career exploration opportunities.
* heard from K-5 principal Jody Schmidt that grade school students had attended an immigration simulation at the Goessel museum and learned how the Mennonite immigrants came to America. Jeremy Voth had given a presentation for grade school students about fire safety. Fifth graders have gone to Starbase in Salina. The Character-Strong focus for the month is Responsibility. 'Family groups' of seven or eight students from different grades met on the half day of school on Sept. 25.
* heard that junior high and high school students also had team-building activities that day that included breakfast, scavenger hunt, identifying career interests, learning styles and suicide prevention.
* heard about illness at the grade school and gratitude for the school nurse.
* heard from Crawford about schools that use donated beef. He wondered if any beef producers in the community would be willing to donate beef to Goessel school or if anyone would sponsor beef donation.
* heard from Crawford about a School Improvement Day that the KESA (Kansas Education Systems Accreditation) team had attended in Hutchinson. Goessel's KESA team includes Crawford, Boden, Schmidt, Heidi Claassen, Janna Duerksen, Chrystiana Miller, Russel Pauls, and Cindy Sattler.

title: Tabor College thriving academically with new & incoming students
author: Hillsboro Free Press
description: After besting a 15-year record for incoming freshman GPA (3.35) in fall 2022, Tabor College continues to build upon its strong foundation in academic performance. With a mark of 3.42 for its newest…
content:
After besting a 15-year record for incoming freshman GPA (3.35) in fall 2022, Tabor College continues to build upon its strong foundation in academic performance. With a mark of 3.42 for its newest freshmen class, Tabor has ushered in three straight classes above 3.40.
Tabor greeted 136 incoming freshmen this semester, helping hit its total of 495 undergraduate students on campus. With 82 students enrolled in graduate and online courses and 44 in dual credit, the college totaled 621 students across all programs. Fall-to-fall retention topped 70% once again, reaching 72% this semester. 'We're continuing to see exceptional students coming to Tabor,' President David Janzen, Ph.D., said. 'After graduating a large class last May, we are very optimistic about our spring transfer class and seeing more students understand why a decidedly Christian education is so valuable. Campus culture is excellent, academics are strong and student activities are thriving.'
Tabor's on-campus and graduate & online students come from 37 U.S. states, 31 countries, and six continents.

title: Area Sports Roundup 10.30.24
author: Hillsboro Free Press
description: Goessel Volleyball - Goessel fell in the sub-state finals to Little River on Saturday, Oct. 26. Scores were as follows: Goessel defeated Colony Crest 25-18, 25-8; Little River defeated Goessel 25-21,…
content:
The Hillsboro High School Cheerleaders participated in High Five Friday at Hillsboro Elementary School where they greeted students with smiles and high fives. Hillsboro's Sutton Redger and Seth Driggers stop the ball on Friday night during the game against Smoky Valley. The Trojans won 21-16. Photo by Josiah Driggers
Goessel
Volleyball – Goessel fell in the sub-state finals to Little River on Saturday, Oct. 26. Scores were as follows: Goessel defeated Colony Crest 25-18, 25-8; Little River defeated Goessel 25-21, 25-20.
Goessel finishes the season 32-8.
Football – The Bluebirds ( 8-man, Division 1, District 3) played at home against Canton-Galva. Canton-Galva won with the final score of 32-24.
The Bluebirds will play at Washington County at 6 p.m. on Thursday, Oct. 31.
Hillsboro
Cross-country – The Trojan girls are State bound! The team placed 3rd at the Regional meet in Marion on Saturday, Oct. 26. Riley Richert led the team with a 3rd place finish in a time of 20:01.62, followed by Quinlyn Funk in 5th place in 20:18.38 and Jaidyn Frantz in 15th place with a PR of 21:05.07. Nora Hein came in with a season PR of 26:03.32, Anna King with a PR of 27:47.07 and Gabi Sibayan with a PR of 34:44.86.
The boys' side had some great races as well, and each of them had a personal best time at this meet. Wyatt Dies led the team in with a time of 19:54.05 which was a PR by over two minutes from the start of the season. Casen Steinert ran a 21:23.27, Ben Werner came in at 22:36.72 and Elijah Holmes ran a 24:18.45 which was over three minutes faster than his first race of the season.
Coming—The Trojan girls will compete at state on Nov. 2 in Wamego.
Football – The Trojans played at home against Smoky Valley on Friday, Oct. 25 and won with a final score of 21-16.
Hillsboro got on the board first when Jesiah Gooch broke off for a 46-yard touchdown run to put the Trojans up 7-0.
With the score 8-7 Smoky Valley, Gooch ran the ball in for Hillsboro from five yards out to put the Trojans up 15-8 after a successful two-point conversion.
The final score of the game came when Zayne Haslett went for a 24-yard run into the endzone to give Hillsboro the edge with just 4 minutes left in the game.
Coming—The Trojans will play against Norton at home at 7 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 1.
Volleyball – The Trojan girls competed in Regionals on Saturday, Oct. 26. The final scores were: Hillsboro defeated Hutch Trinity 25-13, 25-12; Hillsboro defeated Ell-Saline 25-11, 25-16;
Valley Heights defeated Hillsboro 25-17, 25-22.
With the new KSHSAA post-season format in place, the Hillsboro High School Volleyball Team traveled to Blue Rapids to compete in a quad created from the seedings in their region. As the #6 seed, the girls went 2-1 on the night, defeating Hutch Trinity and Ell-Saline, and losing to #3 seed and host, Valley Heights.
As the runner-up of the quad, the Trojans found themselves in the Inman sub-state with the region's #1 seed in the Inman Teutons. After records were submitted, it was determined Hillsboro would meet Inman in the first round. The Teutons were not to be denied and won the contest in two games. With the loss, the Trojans finish their season with a 25-14 record.
'It was hard to end the season the way we did, but it was a season of growth and building for our team. We had girls playing new positions, girls learning to carry more responsibility and girls on the varsity court for the first time. The team had some big wins throughout the season—including wins over Hesston, Hoisington, Little River and Concordia—and several of their losses to high-level teams were within a few points. They won the Douglass tournament, finished second at the Southeast of Saline tournament and got 3rd in the Hillsboro Invitational. The team's strength of schedule was tough but we feel will make us better in the long run—even if that means next season. I am proud of this group and am looking forward to seeing the work they put in to make next season even better,' said Coach Sandy Arnold.
Marion
Cross-country – Marion competed in Regionals on Saturday, Oct. 26.
'For the first time in school history, Marion hosted a Regional XC event. It was a great day for a meet and I am so proud of what we accomplished today as a group and school community. It takes a lot of prep work and great help to pull off an event like this and I am so thankful for everyone who stepped up to help make this day possible,' said Coach Jason Hett.
In the 2A girls' race, Brooklyn Beery ran a season PR and finished in 21st place.
'She ran a great race and has come a long way this season. I am looking forward to three more years as she will continue to grow and be pushed,' said Hett.
Izy Branson also finished her freshman year running a season PR and coming in 35th place.
'She has put in a lot of work, and I am proud of the growth she made this season and looking forward to seeing her continue to grow and mature in this sport,' said Hett. 'Our Lady Warrior runners had a great season and hopefully we will have a full girls team next season.'
Luke Wessel is now a four-time state qualifier with a 3rd-place finish and a season PR personal record) time.
Eli Klenda is now a three-time state qualifier with a 9th-place finish and a season PR.
'In the 2A boys race, our guys were focused and locked in. They knew what they needed to do in order to give themselves a chance on the team side. I could not be more proud of a group of great young men. They laid it all out there today and as a coach, I cannot ask for anything more. Congrats to them both on this achievement,' said Hett.
Harrison Beery ran a great race and a huge PR, finishing in 23rd place.
'He pushed himself to break the wall. Zayden Janzen also had a huge PR and ran his heart out today. He placed 26th. Owen White has been battling an injury the past few weeks and has not run in a meet since Oct 3rd but what heart he showed today. He was hurting the whole race, but did not let that stop him; he gutted out a 37th-place finish today,' said Hett.
Jaxon Salsbury placed 45th running a season PR, and Keenan Lange rounded the team out in 55th place.
'We missed going as a team by three points, but this group can keep their head high as they proved they can do hard things. I am so proud of them for the heart they showed today and the way they represented our school and program today and all season. I am so blessed to get the opportunity to coach this group of great young men,' said Hett.
Coming—Wessel and Klenda will compete at state on Saturday, Nov. 2 at Wamego.

title: Christian Leader wins EPA award
author: Hillsboro Free Press
description: The Christian Leader received a fifth-place award in the Evangelical Press Association Best in Class contest in the 3,001 to 9,000 circulation category. The Christian Leader is the magazine for U.S.…
content:
USMB magazine, Christian Leader, wins 'Best in Class' award for the fifth consecutive year
The Christian Leader received a fifth-place award in the Evangelical Press Association Best in Class contest in the 3,001 to 9,000 circulation category. The Christian Leader is the magazine for U.S. Mennonite Brethren and is headquartered in Hillsboro.
In the Best in Class contest, EPA member publications are grouped by circulation and are invited to enter one issue of their publication to be judged in six areas, including design, use and quality of images, strength of writing and titling and 'overall editorial punch.'
EPA announced the 2024 award winners on Oct. 16.
'This award affirms the work of designer Shelley Kallsen and associate editor Janae Shafer,' said Connie Faber, editor. 'It also recognizes the excellent work of those who write feature department essays and columns, and the contributions of our freelance news writers. I so appreciate each one who helps make the Christian Leader a magazine that U.S. Mennonite Brethren can be proud of.'
Two judges evaluated each entry, with their scores averaged to determine placement. Judges commended the Christian Leader on its 'cohesive and consistent' design and 'simple, eye-catching' cover.
Shelley Kallsen has designed the Christian Leader since she joined the staff of the Hillsboro Free Press. Her design work has been recognized by several EPA awards. The judges also affirmed the editors for the 'strong' theme carried out 'consistently through the issue.'
The Christian Leader was judged on the May/June 2024 issue that focused on Moses' encounter with God recorded in Exodus 3. Writers reflected on God's leading in their lives.
The judges found the theme to be 'appropriate' for the magazine's audience. 'The theme was personally fortifying for me,' wrote one judge.
Up to five awards were made in each of eight categories, with a nearly even number of contestants in each category. For most magazines, contestants compete against a different group of magazines than in the Awards of Excellence contest where competition is divided by type of magazine. In addition to five categories for magazines, Best in Class categories included one for newspapers and two for websites, based on organizational size.
Christian Leader has received an award in the Best in Class contest every year since the contest was introduced in 2020. The magazine received a first-place award in 2022, a third-place award in 2021 and fourth-place awards in 2020 and 2023.
The Evangelical Press Association is a professional organization of Christian print and digital publications: magazines, newspapers, newsletters, and content-driven websites.

title: Goessel student to perform in the Pearl Harbor Memorial Parade
author: Hillsboro Free Press
description: Goessel – Goessel High School (GHS) Cheerleading Captain Brooklyn Wuest will represent Varsity Spirit in the Pearl Harbor Memorial Parade in Honolulu, HI from Dec. 3-9. Cheerleaders and dancers…
content:
Goessel's Brooklyn Wuest will perform in the Pearl Harbor Memorial Parade in Honolulu Dec. 3-9.
Goessel – Goessel High School (GHS) Cheerleading Captain Brooklyn Wuest will represent Varsity Spirit in the Pearl Harbor Memorial Parade in Honolulu, HI from Dec. 3-9.
Cheerleaders and dancers invited to perform in the Pearl Harbor Memorial Parade are part of a select group of All-Americans identified at Varsity Spirit summer camps across the country. All-Americans are based on superior cheerleading or dance skills as well as leadership skills at camps operated by Universal Cheerleaders Association (UCA). Only the top 12% of the cheerleaders and dancers from Varsity Spirit camps earn the chance to participate in a performance of this caliber. The GHS Cheer Squad attended the UCA Cheer Camp at Coffeyville this summer where Wuest was selected as an All-American.
Wuest will perform with Varsity Spirit All-Americans in the parade before thousands of fans lining the streets of Waikiki Beach. This trip marks the 83rd Anniversary of the attack on Pearl Harbor. We honor our veterans and their families while recognizing that once bitter enemies can become loyal friends and allies.
Besides being able to perform for true national heroes, athletes will have the opportunity to meet cheerleaders and dancers from across the nation and enjoy a traditional Hawaiian luau and a memorable trip to the Pearl Harbor Memorial and the USS Missouri Battleship.
Wuest has participated in cheer for four years and gymnastics for 8 years and is often spotted doing flips across the gym floor during time-outs.
Goessel Cheer Coach Raechel Boese said, 'I have seen the years of hard work that Brooklyn has dedicated to being an elite gymnast and cheerleader. Her experience, leadership, and skills play an essential role in the team's chemistry, development and success. I am proud to have coached her and helped her achieve such an accomplishment. I hope this can serve as inspiration for her teammates and all the young girls that look up to her.'
Wuest said, 'I am humbled to receive such a great honor. I'm excited about getting to represent my school and community at this national event; all while getting to do what I absolutely love.'
She continued with a message for all little girls, 'Find what you're passionate about and never give up on it. It doesn't matter where you come from or what you've been through, no dream is too big if you give it your all.'
Wuest will graduate from GHS in May 2025 where she has participated in cheer, volleyball, basketball, track, powerlifting, the school musicals, honors choir and student government. She is the daughter of Joseph Wuest and Dallas and Deena Boese.
If you would like to support Wuest in her journey to represent her community on a national level, you can visit her website at https://bit.ly/3Y56i5A.

title: Goessel School Board considers junior high cross country
author: Cynthia Goerzen
description: The Goessel school board met on Nov. 11 and listened to a request from a 6th grader and a 5th grader for junior high cross country. Currently, Goessel only has cross country for high school students.…
content:
The Goessel school board met on Nov. 11 and listened to a request from a 6th grader and a 5th grader for junior high cross country. Currently, Goessel only has cross country for high school students. Not everyone chooses to play volleyball or football in junior high, and currently there are no other fall athletic options.
It was pointed out that C-team volleyball players only had three games, and 6th graders are not allowed to play football. So there are no fall sports options for 6th grade boys.
The students think a junior high cross-country option would strengthen the high school cross-country program. One junior high student has been running on her own and met her personal goal of 50 miles last summer.
Superintendent Mark Crawford agreed that a junior high cross-country program would increase opportunities for junior high students. He said almost all cross country meets include junior high. He said there is also a league junior high cross country meet.
Board members Sara Hiebert, Bryant Miller, Pat Flaming and Ben Schrag all voiced support for junior high cross country. They felt like it would be wise to build up the cross-country program like the other sports. And they think it will not 'take away' from volleyball and football.
Schrag commented, 'I am in full support of choice and opportunity.'
Crawford said Donna Spoonmore, the high school cross country coach, is excited about the possibility of junior high cross country and would love to have 6th, 7th and 8th graders.
Schrag and Hiebert noted the minimal expense for cross country, commenting that the only expense might be an additional supplemental assistant coach position. Junior high/high school principal Scott Boden said cross-country runners use track uniforms.
Board members thanked the students for coming to the meeting. The board did not vote at this meeting. They will likely vote in December or January.
Turning their attention to another matter, the board heard from Crawford about the 'science of reading' and new requirements for 'letters training' or 'keys to literacy.' Elementary school principal Jody Schmidt mentioned the time commitment for the training. Crawford said a lot of this movement is coming through the state legislature. Flaming and Schrag both commented that it is risky on the part of the state, considering the shortage of teachers.
In other business, the board:
* heard from elementary school principal Jody Schmidt. She commented about the 100% participation at parent-teacher conferences. Some conferences had been rescheduled because of illness.
* heard from Schmidt about the 'attitude of gratitude' currently promoted at the elementary school. Miss Kansas had talked with students about healthy relationships.
* heard from Boden about the 'Build My Future' event hosted by the Wichita Area Builders Association. That was also a day that a number of seniors visited colleges.
* heard from Boden about a 'Reality U' day that students had attended. It was an event to teach them how to budget money for life expenses.
* heard from Schmidt that 3rd grade students placed 1st, 2nd and 3rd in the Marion County Conservation Poster Contest.
* heard from Schmidt that grade school students had a Halloween costume parade in the gym and went trick-or-treating at Bethesda Home and at the high school.
* spent a considerable amount of time discussing transportation needs but made no decision.
* introduced Luke Freeman, who is the new junior high science teacher.
* approved Carol McDaniel as a part-time custodian at the junior high/high school building.
* heard from Boden that 44 junior high students are participating in basketball and 32 high school students.

title: This N That opens new location in Hillsboro
author: Laura Fowler Paulus
description: Mike and Staci Morales live in Hillsboro and own This N That. The family-owned business officially provides repairs to farm tractors and farm equipment of any kind, but they also do semi-truck and…
content:
Staci and Mike Morales own This N That, a family-owned business that specializes in farm tractors and equipment repairs. They have been in business since 2019 on their farm outside of Hillsboro, but are now opening a location in town.
Mike and Staci Morales live in Hillsboro and own This N That.
The family-owned business officially provides repairs to farm tractors and farm equipment of any kind, but they also do semi-truck and trailer repair and automotive work.
'We do a lot of farm repair. We've got a lot of farmers that bring in tractors and balers and swathers and such, and so we take care of that as well. When we move into town, I want to get more into some of the automotive stuff. Light automotive—like brakes and things like that. I want to do brakes and struts and that type of thing on automobiles,' said Mike. 'We're going to grow that side of the business a little bit. Because right now, we have a lot of individual farmers. And we have some customers that bring cars out so we take care of them as well. But the roads are not the best. So that's hindered us a little bit from that aspect. We also do welding, fabricating and weld repairs. We are honest and hardworking and will go above and beyond to satisfy our customers.'
The couple have been operating their business on their farm outside of Hillsboro since 2019, but they are getting ready to open up a new 6,000-square-foot location in town at the corner of Santa Fe and Commercial.
'The business just grew so much, and we needed a bigger location. It will be so much more efficient for the mechanics that we have because we don't have multiple doors where we're at now. But in the new building we can pull semis with the trailer totally in the building,' said Staci.
The couple decided to open a new shop for two reasons—privacy and convenience.
'We have no privacy on the farm anymore. We're very blessed to have all the customers come over, but it's like, we want to get it off the farm. So that's why we came here to our new location,' said Mike. 'And a lot of our customers—like Barkman Honey—they have 35 trailers we take care of. We do all the work for Countryside and Co-op. And we take care of USD 410, all their school buses, and it's just an ideal location for us. It's just going to be better location and facilities-wise.'
The couple are ready for the new facility to be up and running as they are exhausted.
'We had a company put up the building, but we've done most of the sheetrock work, the framework. A lot of the stuff you see in here, we've done ourselves. It's been really tiring. It was a year ago we bought the ground and we weren't going to build on it right away, but we just have gotten so busy and outgrew the facilities at home. We will be glad when this facility is up and running because it's been very tiresome to run a business all day and come up here and work at night,' said Mike. This N That is opening a new location in town on the corner of Santa Fe and Commercial in Hillsboro. They hope to be in their new location this week.
They are in the home stretch finally.
'We will be moved in here if we're approved for occupancy by Wednesday, Nov. 20. We have to have an occupancy inspection, which Ben Steketee, the city inspector, has been very helpful with. Our plan is to move in Thursday or Friday and then kick it off on Monday,' said Mike.
Regardless of which day they open the location, their staff will still be operating at the farm until then.
'During this time, we are still open. The guys are busy working at the farm location. We're still operational and going,' said Mike.
The couple have been married for 25 years and have two teenage boys who attend Hillsboro High School.
'We started out in Newton in the auto mechanic industry. My grandpa was a farmer, and he got us into the Ag side of things. We moved here in 2018 when we bought my grandparents' farm. So we help my uncle farm as well as run the business,' said Staci. 'We love doing both.'
They are thankful to get to do what they do.
'I would like to thank the community for all the help we've received from Hillsboro. I'd like to thank Brent Barkman. He's been with us and guided us through this process,' said Mike. 'And I'd like to thank the man upstairs and our family. They've been putting up with a lot for me being up here.'
The hours will be 8 a.m.- 5 p.m. on Monday through Friday.
The business is certified to offer Department of Transportation inspections for semis and trucks, and they have the diagnostic equipment to have the capability to scan big trucks.
To schedule an appointment or for more information, call Mike at (316)201-8588, email tntfarm99@gmail.com or visit https://www.facebook.com/ThisNThatFarm99.

title: Duell family thankful to Hillsboro
author: Hillsboro Free Press
description: Dear Hillsboro, Nearly 11 years ago we moved our family of four to a tiny little town in a state we had never seen before. And for the next decade plus, we have been loved, supported and cared for by…
content:
Dear Hillsboro,
Nearly 11 years ago we moved our family of four to a tiny little town in a state we had never seen before. And for the next decade plus, we have been loved, supported and cared for by our adopted home.
Now life has taken a new direction that takes us away from Hillsboro but not without a moment of reflection and gratitude. We have been very blessed in the past decade. Our children have grown up, made wonderful friends and had numerous successes in the sports arena, on the stage and in the classroom.
In the midst of a pandemic we welcomed a new family member in a Zoom wedding in our backyard and a couple of years later a new baby girl. We have also suffered through employment challenges, serious illness and the loss of friends and loved ones.
Whether celebrating victories or mourning losses, we have never felt alone. We were immediately welcomed and embraced by Bryce and Sara Wichert and Mark and Karrie Rathbone. In work we have been lifted up by colleagues like Jim Paulus, Ian Thomson, Grant Brubacher, John Wheeler, Ted Turk, Lou Thurston, Dale Dalke, Krista Richert, Eric Driggers and Gina Edwards. As parents we have been inspired by teachers, coaches and church leaders like Phil Oelke, Janet Whisenhunt, Demetrius Cox, Brielle Loewen, Leah Rose and Grant Shewey. These are just a few of so many of you who have blessed our lives.
If a community is measured by how it cares for one another in good times and bad, then Hillsboro can rest in the knowledge that, for this family, you have been an example of God's grace.
Thank you, Hillsboro.
-Nate Duell, Cara Duell, MacKenzie Magee, Brett Magee, Duncan Duell, Ainsley Duell, Angus Duell and Brooklyn Magee

title: Sieberts continue legacy of Diamond X Ranch
author: Laura Fowler Paulus
description: Laramie and Rachel Siebert are the proud owners of Diamond X Ranch located on old Highway 50 between Marion and Hillsboro just past Old Mill Rd. 'The family that has lived on this land goes back four…
content:
Laramie and Rachel Siebert own Diamond X Ranch, a ranch that has been in Laramie's family for four generations. They also own a pasture clearing and fence build business that they run from the ranch. Laramie built the fence behind them.
Laramie and Rachel Siebert are the proud owners of Diamond X Ranch located on old Highway 50 between Marion and Hillsboro just past Old Mill Rd.
'The family that has lived on this land goes back four generations and has been here since the 1870s,' said Laramie.
More recently, Laramie's grandparents Rex and Vernolis Siebert lived on the property and Rex raised and bred registered Hereford bulls.
'He did that out here for many years and traveled all over the United States. In fact, there is a brand wall in our office that we kept the same when we moved here. His grandpa had this wall of wooden shingles. Every time he went out of state somewhere, he'd get their brand branded on this piece of wood, and it's on the wall. One of the brands is 6666 on the Yellowstone show. He was actually there. They're both deceased, so I don't know if he sold them bulls or went and got bulls from them,' said Rachel.
Rex also invented and patented the Spring-O-Matic which has been built and personally tested on the property since 1955. They are still made with quality craftsmanship by Laramie's dad John.
'Those are made in that little shop down in front of our house. It basically looks like a cow shoot. You put a cow or a bull in it, and it flips sideways to hold the cow in there so you can trim their hooves,' said Rachel. 'Eventually my husband will probably make them, but I don't know when that will be.'
Laramie's sister bought the ranch from his grandparents but struggled with drug addiction and destroyed a lot of the property. Laramie and Rachel were able to buy it from her and have been working since then to restore it to its original condition.
They have also kept the brand of Diamond X Ranch the same. But other things have changed.
'We have gotten the ranch back to where it was, but we did lose some of the property. We don't have much property to run cattle, so we decided just that we wanted to start doing the horse thing. My husband has been breaking horses since he was young. He's managed many feed yards. He's been around that all his life. So raising, breeding, training and then selling horses for roping and working is what our plan has been,' said Rachel. 'When they're little, I'll do the groundwork and the round pen, and my husband will break the horses. He used to do a lot of bareback bronc riding and rodeos. He can do a lot of things. He's a pretty well-rounded guy.'
The couple, who have known each other since they were six, own a pasture-clearing and fence-building business called Ranchland Tree Service, LLC.
'We do pasture clearing for farmers that want to clear out big areas of trees to build fence or put cows out. We do big jobs,' said Rachel. 'When we do cut the trees, we cut it even with the ground, and we also spray a chemical on it so that so they won't grow back. We don't charge extra for that. It's included in the cost of the hourly rate to cut the trees.'
Laramie said, 'We specialize in pasture clearing like rangeland so you can utilize your grazing land rather than it being infested with undesirable trees, locusts, hedge, cedar and such. So we come in to clean out and pile it. We also started doing a bunch on the fence building side where there's barbed wire, pipe fence, and and some of those obviously play hand in hand because a lot of old fence rows got trees growing in them, and so we come clear out the trees, tear out the old fence, and build new fence.'
They offer barbed wire, metal or pipe fencing.
'Ranchers or farmers can get a grant through the Farm Service Agency called the EQUIP program. It's a pretty good program. They do a cost share on it, and they cover a lot of costs for clearing rangeland, grassland and grazing ground. It's a pretty good government program to help ranchers and farmers with cost overhead and making the ground more efficient,' said Laramie.
In addition to the ranch and running the business, the couple works outside jobs. Rachel does hair at Silk Salon and Boutique in Marion and Laramie works as a welder at Hillsboro Industries.
'He's been a welder most of his life. His dad has a shop and is a welder and so that's where Laramie learned when he was young. A lot of this fence on our property, he built himself. Where the wagon wheels are he welded all that,' said Rachel. Rachel Siebert designed the pumpkin scene for people to use as a photo prop for photos. She plans to update the spot with a Christmas scene.
Rachel also designed a little area on their property near the road where people can take family photos. She has it decorated for fall with a large pumpkin she made out of a round hay bail. She has a new scene planned for Christmas.
'Anyone can come take pictures in front of it as long as they don't come on the property past it. They can stop there by the mailbox, take pictures by it and then leave,' said Rachel.
Diamond X Ranch is located at 1667 190th in Marion. For more information or to schedule Ranchland Tree Service, LLC for pasture clearing or fence building, call Laramie at 620-381-9002 or visit Ranchland Tree Service LLC on Facebook.
